systems.name: Raw FRI-STARK
systems.note: Plonky3 FRI backend. Proof too large for L1 mainnet — requires L2 verifier contract or off-chain check.

systems.name: Plonky2 (recursive FRI)
systems.note: FRI recursion reduces proof size vs. flat STARK, but verification gas still puts L1 direct-settle out of reach for per-inference use.

systems.name: Halo2 (IPA, no SRS)
systems.note: No trusted setup. Used by ezkl for on-chain ML. Verification gas is tight but workable for occasional settlement; linear verifier complexity.

systems.name: PLONK (BN254 universal)
systems.note: Universal SRS (one ceremony, any circuit). Used by Aztec, gnark. Constant-size proof, sub-400k gas — usable but above the Groth16 floor.

systems.name: Groth16 native (gnark)
systems.note: Lowest on-chain gas (222k). 256-byte proof. But needs a separate MPC ceremony for every new AI circuit — months of setup time per model.

systems.name: SP1 (STARK + Groth16 wrapper)
systems.note: Plonky3 STARK over program execution, then wrapped in Groth16. Measured on Ethereum mainnet: 327,621 gas total (286k verification + 41k calldata/overhead). No per-program setup.

systems.name: RISC Zero (FRI + Groth16 wrapper)
systems.note: STARK (SEAL FRI) over RISC-V execution trace, then SNARK-wrapped. Bonsai proving service. Universal SRS — any RISC-V program proves and verifies for the same fixed gas.

systems.name: Nova fold + wrapper
systems.note: IVC folding: each incremental step costs ~3s prover time, amortizing N steps into a single accumulator. Final Groth16 wrapper settles once on-chain. Ideal for agent step sequences.
